t:
Section 409D(d) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 284h(d)) is amended—
    (1) in paragraph (1), by striking “in consultation with the Director of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and in collaboration with other appropriate national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, may provide for the establishment of” and inserting “in collaboration with the national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, shall support”; and 
    (2) in paragraph (2)(A) and the first sentence of paragraph (2)(E), by striking “may” each place such term appears and inserting “shall”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in collaboration with" signals participation, but the national research institutes and national centers are components of the NIH and so sit inside the federal government. This is intra-government coordination, which the definition excludes. The amendment otherwise only changes "may" to "shall" and adds no public comment, hearing, advisory body with outside members, or right to sue.
fable.s: in collaboration with the national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, shall support

qwen_block.w: The section describes an amendment to a statute that changes the requirement for collaboration between federal entities. The 'Director of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development' and 'other appropriate national research institutes and national centers' are all part of the federal government (specifically, the NIH within HHS). Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_block.s: in paragraph (1), by striking “in consultation with the Director of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and in collaboration with other appropriate national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, may provide for the establishment of” and inserting “in collaboration with the national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, shall support”

opus.w: The only collaboration described is among NIH's national research institutes and national centers, and the consultation being removed was with the NICHD Director. All of these are inside the federal government, so this is coordination within the government, not outside participation. The words "consultation" and "collaboration" are not enough, because no state, expert, company, or member of the public is involved, and the section does not require any rulemaking or hearing.
opus.s: in collaboration with the national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, shall support
opus.b:
The tempting reading is "Yes," because the text uses the words "consultation" and "collaboration." That fails here: every party named is part of NIH, which is a federal agency. The amendment removes the required consultation with the NICHD Director, leaves collaboration among NIH's own institutes and centers, and turns "may" into "shall." No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section mandates collaboration between the Secretary (a federal official) and national research institutes and centers (which are components of the National Institutes of Health, a federal agency). Since all parties involved are inside the federal government, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes consultation or coordination between federal agencies or officials.
qwen_chat.s: in collaboration with the national research institutes and national centers that carry out activities involving pediatric research, shall support
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "collaboration with... national research institutes" constitutes participation because these institutes are distinct entities. However, under the definition, federal agencies and their components (like NIH institutes) are INSIDE the federal government. Coordination between federal entities is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
